exposure: Sonographic estimated fetal weight (EFW) categorized as ≥ 3,800 g or < 3,800 g
cohort: The study included 854 women who delivered macrosomic newborns (actual birth weight ≥ 4,000 g) at a tertiary university-affiliated hospital between 2017 and 2021.
finding: In pregnancies with actual neonatal macrosomia, a larger estimated fetal weight (EFW) was associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery, particularly with primiparity, diabetes, or maternal obesity, without leading to improved maternal or neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Larger estimated fetal weight (EFW) was associated with an increased cesarean delivery rate but a lower operative delivery rate among women with neonatal macrosomia.
birth_weight: Actual birth weight of ≥ 4,000 g for all neonates
